$customNodesComment: EXP-010 AC6, settled 2026-08-28: custom nodes are DELIBERATELY not in this file and not in the picker number, and the statement about them is categorical rather than a percentage. A custom node type comes from a project's own noodl_modules/, so its population is per-project and unbounded — putting it in the numerator inflates a ratio, and putting it in both halves makes the denominator move with whichever project you point the tool at. That is precisely the instance-weighted corpus number this phase spent twelve sessions being misled by (see $comment). Adding these types as `entries` would also be a false claim about the catalog, which is what this file is a ledger OF. The claim instead: a kit's VISUAL nodes (`reactNodes`, i.e. a definition with getReactComponent) export and render; a kit's LOGIC nodes (`nodes`, e.g. tally-kit's whole vocabulary) do not, and every instance of one is named in the report. Both halves are graded by tests/custom-nodes.test.ts, which is the ratchet for this claim.

EXP-011 §55 (session 83): the handle is the id. The Do mints a component-local collection into a state row — const <local> = collection<T>([...items]); set<Row>(<local>); then the Done chain, which reads the array through the local — null until the first Do (the node's Id is empty until then), and every Do mints another. The Id is never a string in the emitted app: the only ports that can take it are the Array Id ports of Array, Insert Object Into Array, Remove Object From Array and Clear Array in the same component, each resolved through one arrayTargetOf (named module | minted handle). An Array bound by wire reads through useCollection(<row> ?? noArray) in render and <row>?.peek() ?? [] in a handler; a mutator bound by wire outside the mint's own chain guards on the handle and raises the runtime's <prefix>/no-array on the error channel before its Failure chain; Remove's row exists only because the handle did. Refuses by name: an Id consumed as a value (the store-its-id-on-an-object pattern), two wires on Items or on an Array Id, an Array Id wired from anything but a mint's Id, Completed consumed (one outcome), Run On Value Change off on the bound Array, a mutator fired both from the mint's Done and from elsewhere.

The back channel: `backAction-<a>` chains run inside the callback under `if (action === 'a')`, AFTER the back-results row is written (navigate.ts flags every backResult output dirty before it sends the signal); a `backResult-<k>` read inside a back chain is the callback's own argument, anywhere else the row (`Record<string, unknown>`, typed unknown — the port is `*`), allocated by a read and refused when the push never attaches. EXP-011 §61 (session 86): `const <local> = popComponent(pageStackEntry, { backAction, results })` per trigger port (Navigate and every wired `backAction-<a>`, as Close Popup compiles per port), the Done arm, and the Failure arm — which raises `pop-component-stack/no-stack-in-scope` on the channel before its chain (the one failure the export can reach; `transition-in-progress` needs a transition). The way back is the reserved prop `pageStackEntry?: PageStackEntryHandle`, passed by the stack row that shows the component and absent everywhere else — the runtime hands the callback to the Pop nodes in the pushed component's OWN scope only (getNodesWithType, non-recursive), and a component shown by Reset or Replace, or placed outside any stack, gets none and answers the runtime's own failure. `result-<k>` values are read where the setters stored them (the handler's render expression); Error is read only inside the Failure arm (`<local>.message`). Emitted as `navigate(...)` with exactly one leading slash, because the runtime compares trimmed paths while react-router reads an unslashed path as relative. ⚠️ navigationPathType is deliberately not consulted: `_getLocationPath` returns the same bare path in both modes and `_getSearchParams` reads `location.search` in both, so the setting chooses only where the same path string is written. §17 (session 46) opened the Open In New Tab arm: `window.open(url, '_blank')` with NO features string, which is the runtime's own call — so its `if (!opened)` return-value test is faithful and works. ⚠️ §15.4 deferred this arm saying the success test was `navigator.userActivation`; that sentence was inherited from External Link and false here — the activation read exists on that node ONLY because it passes `noopener`, which makes `window.open` return null on success as much as on failure (DEF-016). With the arm on, Failure becomes live, Error becomes writable (one static message — the Path gate makes the missing-path write unreachable), and Completed becomes a JOIN beneath both arms rather than a continuation of Done. §18 (session 47) opened the WIRED port too, so Open In New Tab translates in all three of its states — off (`navigate`), on (`window.open`), wired (both).
